open_points.subject: A17 configuration and secret path traversal
open_points.text: each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`, whose presence no code tests (A20 rule 3)
open_points.question: What must happen if the Linux/Python runtime does not expose or honor `O_NOFOLLOW`, given that the kernel must use it but is forbidden to test for its presence?
options: Such a host is outside the release and the process may fail before normal start checks
The kernel must refuse start with a defined reason
The release must name a minimum Linux ABI that guarantees it
open_points.default_guess: Treat `O_NOFOLLOW` as a release prerequisite and refuse start if it cannot be used.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory initialization
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory
open_points.question: Must the data directory, SQLite database, value area and spool already exist, or does the kernel create any missing part; and what happens when only some of them exist?
options: Require the complete initialized layout and refuse otherwise
Create every missing component securely
Require the root directory but create the database and subdirectories
open_points.default_guess: Require an existing private root directory and create missing database and managed subdirectories with private permissions.

open_points.subject: A18 exclusive lock
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start.
open_points.question: What object and locking semantics define this lock, and how are a stale lock file, an unsupported lock operation, or another lock-acquisition error handled?
options: An OS-released advisory lock held for the process lifetime; stale files do not block
A lock-file existence rule requiring stale-lock recovery
Another platform-specific exclusive-lock protocol
open_points.default_guess: Use an OS advisory exclusive lock held by an open descriptor for the process lifetime and refuse start on any acquisition failure except a harmless stale file.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization
open_points.text: Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive
open_points.question: What event establishes arrival order when requests overlap: connection acceptance, first byte, complete message receipt, schema-valid dispatch, or entry into a serialized queue?
options: Order of complete-message receipt
Order of first byte receipt
Order assigned atomically when the surface accepts a complete request
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonically ordered queue position when a complete request is accepted by the MCP surface.

open_points.subject: A18 private filesystem predicate
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: What exact ownership, mode, ACL, hard-link and object-type conditions make the directory and each contained object "private"?
options: Owned by the kernel user with no group/other permission bits
Effective access limited to the kernel user, including ACL checks
Only the data-directory root is checked; managed children are trusted
open_points.default_guess: Require every managed object to be owned by the kernel user, reject special objects, and allow no group/other permission bits or ACL access.

open_points.subject: A18 post-start permission changes
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise. Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written.
open_points.question: Are ownership and permission checks repeated on later store calls as the symlink check is, and what happens if an object becomes non-private after startup?
options: Recheck every opened component and fail that store call with nothing written
Check privacy only at startup
Stop the kernel when later permission or ownership drift is found
open_points.default_guess: Recheck ownership, type and permissions when opening each managed path and fail the store call without writes on drift.

open_points.subject: A18 secure path traversal
open_points.text: Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links
open_points.question: Does A18 require component-by-component descriptor-relative traversal with `O_NOFOLLOW`, as the changed A17 now explicitly requires, or only a no-follow check on the final file?
options: Use `O_NOFOLLOW` on every path component
Use no-follow only on the final component
Resolve and scan the tree at startup, then trust directory paths
open_points.default_guess: Open every component descriptor-relative with `O_NOFOLLOW` and require intermediate components to be directories.

open_points.subject: A18 database and filesystem crash consistency
open_points.text: Every change is one call to the store module and one transaction inside it; callers never open, name or pass a transaction. A call that fails writes and changes no record; the only trace it can leave is a published file no record names.
open_points.question: What durability and ordering guarantee must hold across the SQLite commit and publication of one or several files if the process or host crashes, especially whether a committed record may ever name a missing or incomplete file?
options: Records may never name missing or incomplete files; only unreferenced complete files may remain
Process crashes may leave records naming missing files and startup repairs them
Atomicity is guaranteed only for ordinary call failures, not crashes
open_points.default_guess: Publish and durably sync complete files before committing their references, so crashes can leave only complete unreferenced files, never dangling records.

open_points.subject: A18 meaning of flushed and durable
open_points.text: written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place
open_points.question: Does "flushed" require an OS durability operation on the file and containing directory, and when may a successful store call be acknowledged relative to SQLite and filesystem synchronization?
options: Durably sync the file, rename, sync the directory, commit and durably sync SQLite before success
Flush only user-space buffers; process-crash safety is sufficient
Durability settings are an implementation choice
open_points.default_guess: Require file and directory synchronization plus durable SQLite commit before acknowledging success.

open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup failures
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool ... are removed; nothing else is. A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start
open_points.question: Does failure to enumerate or remove a temporary file or unreferenced value byte stop startup, get ignored like an unremovable obsolete spool directory, or leave the object quarantined?
options: Refuse startup
Continue and leave every unremovable orphan unserved
Continue only for obsolete spool directories; refuse for temporary and value areas
open_points.default_guess: Continue only for obsolete spool cleanup failures, but refuse startup if temporary or unreferenced value cleanup cannot be completed safely.

open_points.subject: A18 existing content at a digest path
open_points.text: Equal bytes are stored once. A completed file a record names is never overwritten
open_points.question: When a digest path already exists, must the kernel verify its type, size and digest before reuse, and what happens if the existing bytes do not match?
options: Verify on every reuse and fail without writes on mismatch
Trust any existing regular file at the digest path
Verify the whole content area only at startup and refuse on corruption
open_points.default_guess: Verify the existing regular file before reuse and treat any mismatch as a store failure that stops the kernel after the internal-error response.

open_points.subject: A18 store format across releases
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record
open_points.question: How does a release recognize the database schema and filesystem-layout version, and what must it do with a store created by an older, newer or incompatible release?
options: Perform an explicit transactional migration for supported older versions and refuse others
Require an exact store-format match and refuse every mismatch
Open compatible schemas without a recorded format version
open_points.default_guess: Record a store-format version, migrate explicitly supported older formats transactionally, and refuse newer or unknown formats.

open_points.subject: A20 definition of supported Linux host
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: What exactly counts as a supported Linux host—kernel/ABI floor, CPU architecture, libc, distribution, containers, WSL or Android—and is compatibility with every such host promised or only with hosts satisfying unstated prerequisites?
options: Name a tested kernel, architecture and userspace support matrix
Support any Linux able to run the pinned interpreter, dependencies and bubblewrap probes
Treat `Linux` only as a build-target label with no runtime compatibility promise
open_points.default_guess: Support Linux hosts that can run the release's pinned interpreter and runtime and pass all explicit startup checks, while rejecting other operating-system kernels.

open_points.subject: A20 Linux-only enforcement
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host
open_points.question: Is non-Linux exclusion enforced by packaging/build selection or by a kernel startup check, and if a binary is executed on an unsupported host, what observable failure and check precedence apply?
options: Do not produce a runnable artifact for other hosts
Perform a first startup check and refuse with a defined reason
Allow dependency or sandbox startup checks to fail incidentally
open_points.default_guess: Enforce it both in release packaging and as the first runtime startup check, refusing before opening the store or surface.
